# Master Summary
## Global Education Models and Structural Challenges
Educational systems globally range from centralized, secular frameworks in France, Ireland, and Turkey to developing nations grappling with equity and resource disparities. France and Turkey utilize distinct pathways, with Turkey recently integrating vocational apprenticeships while facing controversy over curriculum changes. In contrast, developing nations like Nigeria, Ghana, and Sri Lanka struggle with outdated curricula, teacher shortages, and deep socioeconomic divides, though Israel stands out for its high scientific attainment and mobility. Meanwhile, Sweden and Norway prioritize equity through state funding and non-graded structures, respectively, despite challenges with immigrant integration and accessibility gaps in upper secondary education.

# Master Summary
## Regional Dynamics and Emerging Trends
Asia presents diverse approaches to international engagement and curriculum design. Taiwan maintains a rigorous, exam-oriented model with mandatory English instruction and tracks students into specific academic paths, hosting a significant number of mainland students. Hong Kong has evolved into a bilingual system where English-medium instruction correlates with prestige, though political shifts like the 2020 National Security Law have triggered student exodus and necessitated historical narrative revisions. Similarly, Indonesia operates a 12-year compulsory framework integrating religious institutions, while Egypt faces severe qualitative deficits driven by low salaries and infrastructure issues, leading to heavy reliance on private tutoring and a skills mismatch.
